text:
marta: Heads-up — finishing the analysis for next quarter's Dedicated commits. Seeing a noticeable mismatch between reserved vGPU hours and actual peak throughput in eu-west1 :thinking:
ian: Can you share the raw numbers? committed GPUs vs observed 95th pctl?
marta: Commit: 120 A100-equivalents in eu-west1 + 40 in us-west1. Observed 95th pctl throughput (Feb–Mar): eu-west1 ~85 A100-eq, us-west1 ~55 A100-eq. Cloud bill shows us-west1 burst charges on March 7th.
raj: Uploaded the export to S3. Quick query I ran:
```
SELECT region, SUM(billed_gpu_hours) AS hours
FROM billing_export
WHERE service = 'GPU' AND month = '2026-03'
GROUP BY region;
```
raj: Result: eu-west1 62k hrs, us-west1 48k hrs, ap-south1 9k hrs (spikes from tests).
sanjay: So eu-west1 committed 120 but used 62k hrs -> equivalent committed hours are 120 * 24 * 31 = ~89k hrs, so utilization ~70% for eu-west1. us-west1 looks undercommitted given bursts.
elaine: Finance flagged a $28k one-off billing line for premium GPUs in us-west1 on Mar 7th — likely preemptible fallback failure.
marta: My read: we overcommitted eu-west1 by ~15–20% if we want 90% utilization target, but undercommitted us-west1 for burst tolerance. Current contracts charge us for full capacity; we should consider rebalancing commits by region and adding a small burst buffer.
ian: What SLAs drive the burst need in us-west1? Are customers pinned to region or using smart-routing?
sanjay: Most enterprise Dedicated customers request regional affinity. We also have smart-routing but it prefers region-local for latency-sensitive routes. That makes local capacity planning important.
marta: Proposal: reduce eu-west1 commit to 100 A100-eq, increase us-west1 to 60, and add a shared burst pool of 10 A100-eq in central region (us-central) for cross-region overflow. This keeps committed total roughly balanced while matching usage patterns.
elaine: Financially, moving 20 A100-eq from eu-west1 to us-west1 should shave ~8% off carry cost assuming current discounts — but we need to check early-termination or migration fees.
raj: I'll run a 12-month cost simulation with current price curves + expected growth 15% q/q and output pv/cost. Anyone object to me including 3 scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive)?
ian: Do it. Also include impact if we allow 10% sudden burst to be served by on-demand at market spot rates vs committed.
sanjay: Note: GPUs in us-west1 have fewer quota limits but higher spot preemption rates. For burst pool, consider replicating critical model states across regions to avoid cold-start KV warming.
marta: Good call. Add a note: measure KV warm-up time for 8B vs 70B models — if >90s, on-demand bursts may violate latency SLOs.
deploy-bot: deployment: infra/region-config updated by marta — diff includes proposed commit shuffle, awaiting approvals.
elaine: Approving pending cost simulation. If simulation shows <3% net increase over 12 months with better SLO compliance, finance signs off.
marta: Thanks — action items: raj runs sim (ETA 48h), sanjay drafts migration playbook for moving capacity, ian to validate SLA mapping and routes, elaine to confirm contract amendment constraints.
ian: Also add a telemetry check: alert if regional utilization crosses 85% for 3 consecutive 10m windows so we can trigger pre-emptive routing.
sanjay: I can add that to the infra SLOs.
marta: Perfect. Back to the spreadsheet after raj's run. :thumbsup:
